title: Checkpoint Tuning & WAL Generation Spikes: Eliminating I/O Spikes
realWorldScenario: Every 5 minutes, database write latency spikes from 1.5ms to 850ms for 30 seconds. System telemetry shows 100% disk write bandwidth saturation coinciding with PostgreSQL log messages: `LOG: checkpoints are occurring too frequently (30 seconds apart)` and `checkpoint starting: time`.
questionStatement: Explain the PostgreSQL Checkpoint mechanism. What triggers a checkpoint (`checkpoint_timeout` vs `max_wal_size`)? How does checkpoint spreading (`checkpoint_completion_target`) smooth out disk I/O, and what are full-page writes (`full_page_writes`) after a checkpoint?
expectedConcepts: Dirty page flushing from shared_buffers to persistent storage
full_page_writes (FPW) preventing torn pages after crash
Write amplification caused by frequent checkpoints
hints: What happens when dirty pages are dumped all at once versus smoothed over the interval?
Why does PostgreSQL write an entire 8KB page image into WAL on its first modification after checkpoint?
What parameter should be increased when logs say checkpoints are occurring too frequently?
